newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Roche first-half sales up 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Roche first-half sales up 20 percent.

text.p: Roche Holding AG sales volume moved into higher gear in the second quarter, joining forces with the weak Swiss franc to produce a 20 percent jump in first-half group turnover, the company said on Tuesday.

Analysts hailed the underlying six percent growth rate measured in local currencies in the first six months, which was double the pace in the first quarter and helped boost sales in the semester to 9.30 billion Swiss francs.

Roche's non-voting participation certificates rose on the sales news and the Basle-based drug company's forecast that 1997 profit would rise, excluding acquisitions-related provisions. But they turned easier in a generally weaker market.
"Roche anticipates another good result for the year. Before extraordinary provisions related to acquisitions, Roche expects a further increase in income," it said without elaborating.
Analysts said the six percent advance in local-currency terms should help the company's participation certificates advance in the short term.

Roche certificates have lagged the blue-chip Swiss Market Index by around 10 percent over the past six months, and trailed the Swiss chemical sector index -- dominated by Novartis -- by some 12 percent over the same period.
Certicates were up 60 Swiss francs to 14,345 around 1210 GMT, off a high of 14,435.
"I would say overall these are encouraging results. Certainly they are an improvement on the first quarter, which is good," Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Genghis Lloyd-Harris said from London.
"Pharmaceuticals were slightly stronger than we had expected, but there really is nothing that leaps off the page here," he said.
Zurich Cantonal Bank analyst Meinrad Gyr also seized on the pharmaceutical sales, which like overall turnover rose six percent in local currency and 20 percent in Swiss francs.
"(This is) a significant improvement, but not yet the level of Novartis," he wrote in a research note. He upgraded Roche to buy from hold.
Gilbert Puder, at Bank Sarasin in Basle, said the results were clearly above his expectations, especially for drugs.
He said sales growth of around 18 percent was possible in the second half, but he noted the weak Swiss franc was distorting the headline number.

"I think the share price short term will be above market," he said, though he added relative performance was difficult to gauge when the Swiss market was already so high in historical terms and from a valuation point of view.
Roche said the pharmaceutical sales growth rate increased despite generic competition after the expiry of patent protection for its anti-epilepsy drug Rivotril.

Its top-selling prescription drugs continued to show double-digit growth, while sales of AIDS drug Invirase and CellCept, used in transplant medicine, more than doubled compared with the first half of 1996.

Roche said a regulatory review of its Posicor hypertension drug, Xenical anti-obesity drug and Tasmar, for treating Parkinson's Disease, was proceeding on schedule and its sales force had been substantially expanded for the product launches.
Analysts said Posicor was being launched now in the United States and would start in Europe in September. Puder said Xenical and Posicor had nearly the same timetable.
"Half-year sales for the OTC (non-prescription) business were also up by two figures," Roche said.

Sales of vitamins and fine chemicals rose 16 percent in Swiss francs and three percent in local currencies. Demand in Europe and North America was restrained, but growth was strong in China, Latin America and southeast Asia.
Diagnostics sales were up 27 percent in Swiss francs and 15 percent in local currencies, well ahead of the market average.

Turnover in fragrances and flavours swelled 25 percent in Swiss francs and 12 percent in local terms. Roche consolidated sales of its Tastemaker unit from April. Its takeover of Tastemaker was approved on March 31, making it the world's largest supplier of flavours.
Roche said it would publish a detailed half-year report in mid-August.
